WhatsApp is developing a new feature that allows users to connect third-party AI agents to the app, chat with them, and instruct them to perform tasks on their behalf. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing support for third-party agents

When platforms like OpenClaw first took off, one of the main ways users controlled them remotely was by connecting agents to instant messaging apps.

However, many users later discovered that configuring bots and third-party AI agents on WhatsApp could lead to their WhatsApp accounts being banned.

Meanwhile, Telegram capitalised on this trend and became one of the main platforms for users to communicate with or issue commands to agents, which could run on users' local computers or be deployed in the cloud.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is introducing native support for third-party AI agents, allowing users to connect agents directly to designated chat windows within the app.

After users set up a new bot on WhatsApp, the app generates an API key that users can use to connect the agent to the chat window. WABetaInfo explains: "The specific steps depend on the platform, but most services have a field where users can paste" the API key, enabling direct conversations with third-party agents through WhatsApp.

Below is WABetaInfo's report:

The site noted that only some Android users currently have access to this new feature, but it is expected to roll out more widely in the short term. WABetaInfo stated that WhatsApp's implementation supports up to five agents per account and allows users to customise the name and profile picture of each agent. However, chats with third-party agents do not currently offer end-to-end encryption.
